title: Benchmark harness: runner fan-out and dataset lifecycle for stable profile publishing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: When onboarding new models we publish performance profiles that must be repeatable and comparable across versions. Current harness behavior mixes dataset sampling, multi-runner execution, and artifact publication in ad-hoc steps which leads to non-deterministic profiles and noisy regressions. Goal: Rework benchmark harness pipeline to separate dataset lifecycle (intake, canonicalization, stable sampling), runner fan-out (isolated shards, deterministic random seeds, resource tags), and a formal profile-publish step with provenance metadata. Deliver a minimal migration that preserves current eval coverage but produces stable, verifiable profiles suitable for version pinning and automated rollouts. Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end pipeline runs produce bit-identical prompt-to-score mappings for a seedable run across at least 95% of sampled prompts. 2) Published profiles include dataset snapshot id, prompt-version hash, runner image id, seed, and aggregated latencies/throughput. 3) A new "dry-run + compare" mode that shows delta between candidate and baseline profiles. 4) Backward-compatible artifacts so Console and Optimize can consume new profile schema without breaking. Scope: - Dataset lifecycle: intake validators, canonical prompt normalization, deterministic sampler with stratified buckets. - Runner fan-out: implement shard coordinator that pins runner shards to GPU types and sets per-shard seed; isolate KV cache effects between shards. - Profile publish: create provenance envelope and a lightweight signature (sha256) for profile artifacts and attach to model metadata. Out of scope: new dataset UI in Console (will be follow-up). Risks & mitigations: - Non-determinism from external RNGs: run reproducibility tests, pin numpy/torch/random seeds and record library versions. - Performance regressions due to isolation: add microbenchmarks for overhead and allow opt-in isolation via config. Implementation plan: 1) Prototype deterministic sampler as library used by harness (ENG-71890 infra dependency). 2) Add shard coordinator and seed propagation in runner orchestration layer. 3) Extend profile manifest schema and publish step. 4) Add CLI flags for dry-run/compare and integrate with existing eval orchestration. 5) Add end-to-end tests, and a migration job to re-publish stable profiles for top-10 model families. Datasets & prompts: incorporate per-dataset canonicalization rules (strip trailing whitespace, normalize unicode, stable tokenization seeds). Outputs: PR to realtime-harness, updated profile manifest spec, migration playbook, and a demo run used for validation.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Kickoff: scoped initial spike to deterministic sampler. Spike found that tokenizers produced non-deterministic offsets for multiline prompts; decision: normalize newline characters and run byte-level hashing pre-tokenization.
2025-02-20 - Design review with PM (Alyssa Park) and Design (Ravi Iyer): agreed on provenance fields and minimal signature scheme. Action: add 'profile_manifest_v2' field to store new schema.

2025-02-25 - Implementation note: created prototype coordinator in branch feat/runner-shards-coordinator (https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-harness/pull/1983). Coordinator currently supports N shards + per-shard seed propagation but needs KV isolation instrumentation.

2025-02-28 - QA: ran 30 deterministic replays of sample dataset 'webqa-v2' and observed 92% identical score-to-prompt mapping; investigating remaining variance (likely from model-variant selection in fallback logic).

2025-03-03 - Review feedback from infra (Lena Shah): requested explicit library version recording in profile_manifest; added 'python_packages' field to manifest and pinned numpy/transformers versions in harness container.
2025-03-05 - Next: implement dry-run compare CLI and wire Console ingestion hook for profile_manifest_v2. Owner: Diego. ETA for next demo: 2025-03-18.
notes: This ticket is a bridge between the eval/harness team and runtime infra; coordinate change windows with Dedicated platform team to avoid producing incompatible published profiles during the migration window. Use feature-flag 'profile_publish_v2' for staged rollout.
